Hi Jane,

Thanks for the PDF — this is helpful. Short answer up front: we prefer vendors use the portal for anything that needs PO matching and automated processing; email is an acceptable fallback for one-off or low-volume vendors.

I pulled together a short decision matrix and the must-have fields so your export team can map them. See notes below and I’ve attached a one-page matrix (invoicing_channel_matrix.pdf).

Decision highlights (summary):
- Portal: best for PO matching, automatic 2-way/3-way match, faster payment cycles when PO is present, structured attachments accepted (XML/CSV/UBL).
- Email: ok for non-PO invoices, small ad-hoc invoices, or when portal access is not available. Manual ingestion increases review time and exception rates.

Mandatory invoice fields (for both channels):
- Redwood PO number (exact match)
- Invoice number (unique)
- Invoice date (ISO yyyy-mm-dd)
- Line-level description, quantity, unit price, line total
- Vendor legal name and Redwood vendor ID (if provided)
- Billing remittance address and bank details or remittance email
- Tax IDs (country-specific)

Optional but recommended: currency, payment terms code, project/code field, shipping amount broken out.

Attachments referenced in portal: we can accept CSV/UBL/JSON attachments for line-level parsing. For email: a single PDF is fine but please add a CSV with line breakdown when PO matching is required.

Next step: Karthik and Mina, can you confirm if there are any additional finance/procurement constraints (PO stamping, minimum invoice amounts that must use portal, exceptions)? If everything looks good I’ll share a short vendor-facing checklist Jane can use.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: invoicing_channel_matrix.pdf]

Thanks Marissa — quick procurement perspective:

- Portal is strongly preferred for any invoice tied to a PO. Our AP system auto-matches PO -> invoice if the PO number is in the designated field and the vendor ID matches. Portal submissions reduce manual routing and exceptions by ~60% based on last-year metrics.
- We need a defined fallback: if a vendor emails an invoice for a PO, AP will triage manually but the vendor should include the PO in the email subject and attach a line-level CSV to speed processing.
- Minimum threshold: for US vendors, invoices < $250 may be accepted by email without portal access, but they must still include vendor ID and remittance details.

I suggest we publish a two-row table on the onboarding doc: (1) Portal required for PO invoices >= $250 or recurring billing; (2) Email allowed for non-PO and < $250 with required fields.

Karthik
Sr. Procurement Manager

Adding finance requirements -- thanks for drafting this. A couple of operational must-haves to include in the vendor checklist: 

- Required invoice header fields (we need exact header labels if vendors will export from ERP):
  - "PO Number"
  - "Invoice Number"
  - "Invoice Date"
  - "Line Description"
  - "Qty"
  - "Unit Price"
  - "Line Total"
  - "Tax Amount"
  - "Invoice Total"

- For CSV/portal payloads: use UTF-8, comma-delimited, include header row matching the exact labels above.
- Preferred remittance: remittance@acme-payments.com (we'll map this to our AP routing).
- Exception handling: if the PO cannot be found during automated match, AP will route to a reviewer and payment will be delayed until a resolution note is added. We ask vendors to include an internal contact and purchase order PDF when available.

I attached a short CSV with example rows (sample_invoice_rows.csv) so their export team can mirror column order.

Mina Haddad
